papers.title: Dissecting an Unexplored SASS Control-Code Field: Barrier Exemption and Programmable Warp Priority
authors: Ziwen Wang, Qi Luo, Kunlin Li, Changxi Liu, Dongsheng Wang, Yun Chen
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.24437v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Every instruction in NVIDIA's native GPU ISA (SASS) carries a control code that guides hardware scheduling, and prior work has decoded its known fields to optimize GPU kernels. However, one control-code field remains unexplored: it appears over 500000 times in NVIDIA's closed-source libraries such as cuBLAS and cuDNN, yet nvcc never emits it when compiling user programs. This paper presents the first systematic study of this control-code field across GPU architectures from Volta to Blackwell. papers.title: TechReport: Implementing CHERI in gem5
authors: Philipp Schmitz, Vishwas Vasuki Gautam, Tobias Jauch, Anna Lena Duque Ant\'on, Johannes M\"uller, Dominik Stoffel, Wolfgang Kunz
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.24460v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Despite countless mitigation efforts, memory safety issues still prevail. The recently discovered security issues in PHP underline this fact. One of the most promising approaches to solving this problem is the concept of Capability Hardware Enhanced RISC Instructions (CHERI). There is a well-developed ecosystem of ISA simulators, compilers, operating systems, and hardware designs that support CHERI. However, the lack of a simulator modeling microarchitectural detail hinders efficient and fast design space exploration for CHERI-enhanced designs means the performance impact of CHERI remains understudied. papers.title: MicroAssert: Microarchitecture-Aware Structured Assertion Generation for CPU Verification
authors: Hongqin Lyu, Yonghao Wang, Zhiteng Chao, Wenxing Li, Tiancheng Wang, Evangeline F. Y. Young, Huawei Li
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.24872v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Automatic assertion generation reduces manual verification effort, yet existing approaches struggle to capture microarchitectural behaviors and cross-region interactions in CPUs. We present MicroAssert, a microarchitecture-aware framework that identifies functional regions directly from RTL and generates local and composite assertions through structured contracts and deterministic verification primitives. Coverage-guided feedback further improves verification completeness by progressively expanding proof-relevant RTL coverage. papers.title: BeFit: Shifting Complexity from Weights to Bernstein Activations for Resource-Constrained Sensing
authors: Malak Gamal El-Din, Yasser Shoukry, Salma Elmalaki
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.23520v1 Announce Type: cross
